correctness.rationale: For the identity matrix and an exact orthogonal projector of rank m, the new independent normalized Gaussian residual block has squared Frobenius norm chi-square(b*m)/b, conditionally independent of earlier outcomes. This gives the finite first-success product including the rank-zero endpoint and the exact false-acceptance probability. Stirling/gamma-density moderate deviations uniformly on sqrt(q log q) windows and Chernoff truncation convert the hazard sum to sqrt(2q)/b^(3/2) times an integrated normal tail. At beta solving beta^2+4 log beta=log(q/(pi*b^3)), this sum tends to exp(-x), squared hazards vanish, and the survival product tends to exp(-exp(-x)). Last-block-only pruning changes the rank by at most b=o(sqrt(q)/(beta)), so Slutsky transfers the law. Exact orthogonality, scalar threshold, block-grid and fixed-b assumptions are explicit. Executed standalone numerical code passed 784 finite consistency, QR and numerical comparisons. No finite experiment substitutes for the asymptotic argument.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper defines the fresh-block normalized Gaussian estimator and rank-pruning algorithm, but the inspected proof, algorithm and experimental sections do not supply the exact identity-spectrum sequential first-success law or its Gumbel fluctuations. Earlier private claim 88fc5e21-b8ad-4125-8a76-f940bc870968 establishes a leading sqrt(n log n) shortfall for unit-block *relative* threshold with a random cumulative denominator; the leading qualitative pathology is prior work and is not claimed here. A block-general exact *absolute* finite law and second-order Gumbel normalization do not follow by implication from that claim. A 2018/2019 HSS stopping preprint gives marginal Gaussian concentration with a different rule; the 2023 LUPP interpolative-decomposition preprint uses a Schur-complement estimator; 2026 shared-probe certification analyzes reuse of validation and calibrated stopping rather than newly generated uncalibrated QB blocks. Mathematical-record searches for source title, stopping law aliases, Gumbel, block width and chi-square found no claimed equivalent; nonindexing remains a risk, not a novelty proof.

value.rationale: For the explicit matrix-free fresh-block randomized QB stopping rule, the full exact finite stopping distribution enables calibrated failure risk computation, and the nontrivial Gumbel limit supplies a sharp second-order quantile correction beyond existing leading unit-block estimates. The result reveals a sequential multiple-inspection issue left unresolved by an unbiased one-step indicator. Block width changes failure risk at finite n, while any fixed b eventually has false acceptance probability one; last-block pruning does not repair it. This identifies a motivated, actionable mathematical boundary of randomized rank determination. The theorem intentionally does not imply significant relative error excess, since the actual relative miss vanishes, or provide guarantees for general spectra.
